title: same-named foreign copies of the faces the suite opens, priced by launch directory
verdict_reason: 10 of 218 literal faces have at least one same-named copy with different bytes in a directory a reader could be launched from; 6 of those are a generic basename shared by several faces (latest.json) and 4 use a name only one face carries; 0 of the exposed names is read by a bare literal in smoke_test.py, so 0 would land on a different document.
method_limits: one directory level per candidate dir: a bare read of the basename can only land on a file directly inside the launch directory, so deeper copies are not shadows for this shape.
the CLI home and the fleet siblings are read from this host's layout; a path that does not exist is published with exists=false and contributes nothing.
the impact class compares top-level key sets only, never values: same_top_level_keys means the reader would meet a document of the same shape, not the same numbers.
the bare-literal join reads smoke_test.py string constants equal to the basename; a reader that builds the name from a variable is invisible to it.
templated faces (%s/*) are excluded from the shadow test and listed separately: a template has no single basename to shadow.
this study excludes its own artefact names from the candidate index by pointing the shadow test at E411's population, which predates SHADOWFACE-*.

own_sha is a snapshot of the bytes compared at generation time: producers rewrite their faces every round, so verify re-derives the classification and the shadow paths but never equality-gates a stored sha (E420 family -- a number that moves on an honest rebuild cannot be a gate).
